title: Consent Management & Data Governance
html:
A CDP without governance is a liability. Data 360's consent model, data spaces, retention, access controls, and audit trails are exam staples and the difference between production-ready and dangerous implementations. This phase covers consent categories and the Consent API, privacy workflow, retention, sharing, and the lab's ConsentManagementService + Consent_Preference__c.

Learning Objectives

By the end of this phase, you will be able to:

  • Configure consent categories and capture opt-in/opt-out from any channel.
  • Use the consent model and consent API concepts to filter segmentation and activation.
  • Apply data retention policies to DLOs/DMOs and explain their data-availability consequences.
  • Design access control with data spaces, permission sets, and sharing.
  • Reason about the ethics and audit trail the Data 360 consultant must implement.

1. Consent: the model

Data 360 stores consent preferences per person, per category. You will configure which consent categories your org uses (Email, SMS, Phone, Advertising, Data Sharing with Partners…), each with an opt-in state and a source/time-of-capture.

Object/mechanismRole
Consent categoryA named channel/use (Email, SMS, Advertising)
Consent captureAn opt-in/out event with source (form, agent, API), date, portal
Consent propagationActivation/segment filters use the category state to include/exclude members
Consent AttributionRecords why/when consent was given (audit + preferences)

The Consent API lets you record captures programmatically (from web forms, apps, and external systems), so every channel feeds the same preference store. This is the "single source of consent" the exam wants you to recommend over channel-local preference databases.

2. Consent-gated segmentation and activation

The governance discipline runs through Phases 6 and 7:

  1. Segments should include only individuals with the relevant consent when the use case requires it (marketing sends, ads).
  2. Activations enforce suppression by consent category at publish time (Phase 7 §4).
  3. Withdrawal flows: an unsubscribe in Marketing Cloud must flow back into Data 360 (suppressed = true) so the next segment/activation honors it automatically.

Lab mirror — ConsentManagementService:

apex
public with sharing class ConsentManagementService {
    public static void setConsent(Id contactId, String category, Boolean optIn) { ... }
    public static Set<Id> consentedContacts(Set<Id> candidates, String category) { ... }
    // ActivationSyncService calls consentedContacts() before publishing.
}

The service: upserts the Consent_Preference__c row (one DML), keeps a candidate→consented set, and lets ActivationSyncService do the suppression math you tested in Phase 7.

3. Data retention

  • Retention periods are configured per DLO/DMO (and by data-usage type). After the period, Data 360 purges the stored records.
  • The catch: retention that is too short silently weakens your unified profiles, segments, and history-aware insights ("why did my lifetime-value insight drop overnight? — because 13-month-old orders were purged").
  • Set retention per data space/object to match business need AND regulatory minimum (you can't legally delete chat history you later need for a GDPR request, but you may want to purge ad log data).

Retention is where consultants most often surprise their own stakeholders. Recommend a table and a review cadence, and keep audit/reporting DMOs in a separate, longer-retention space.

4. Access control & sharing

LayerWhat it protectsConfig
Data spaceContainment/isolation of data + metadataCreate separate spaces per business unit/use case
Permission setsWho can build/segment/activateData 360 Admin / Marketing Admin / Marketing Viewer
Object-level securityWhich DMOs a role can seeGrant via Data 360 permission set + object/field permissions
Record sharing / data actionsWhich data actions fire and for whomActivation/action-level filters and targets

Governance architecture note (verified 2026): a regulated multi-space design exposes only a filtered view of the identity graph to the operational (e.g. customer-success) space — the marketing-held identity universe stays partitioned in its own data space. Design spaces first, then flows, segments, and agents against the least-privileged view.

5. Ethics, lineage, and audit

  • Data lineage — Data 360 tracks source → DLO → DMO → insight → segment → activation, giving every consumer the "how did this field get here" answer.
  • Trust/ethics — the Data 360 consultant is accountable for: transparency (tell people what you collect), proportionality (only the data the use case needs), and fairness (segments that don't discriminate).
  • Audit trail — activation runs, consent captures, and data-action executions are the artifacts regulators ask for. Keep them; this lab's Activation_Audit__c and Consent_Preference__c model exactly those artifacts.

Hands-On Exercises

Exercise 1: Consent capture design

Design the consent flow for a telco web self-service: which categories, which capture sources (form + call-center agent + API), how a withdraw-all is represented, and how you prevent email marketing after a withdraw.

Exercise 2: Suppression trace

Trace a member: consent=Email(opt-out), segment includes them (data consent OK), activation publishes to MCE. What stops the send? Walk ConsentManagementService.consentedContacts + ActivationSyncService logic and state the three audit numbers that result.

Exercise 3: Retention review

An airline retains web-event DLO for 90 days but needs 24-month "membership tier" DMOs. Propose the retention policy set (which objects, which periods, which space) and predict what breaks if the DMO retention is set to 30 days.

Exercise 4: Lab test

Extend ConsentManagementServiceTest: capture consent for 3 contacts across 2 categories, assert consentedContacts returns only the matching category, then withdraw one and assert suppression removes them from the published set.

Key Terms Glossary

TermDefinition
Consent categoryA channel/use (Email, SMS, Advertising) with an opt-in state.
Consent captureAn opt-in/out recording (source, date, portal).
Consent APIAPI for recording consent captures from any system.
Consent propagationThe way consent state flows into segments and activations.
Data retentionPer-object time rule after which records are purged.
Data lineageTrackable path source → DLO → DMO → insight → segment → activation.
Data space isolationThe data-space boundary that enforces least-privilege data view.
SuppressionRuntime exclusion of non-consenting members at activation.

Certification Checkpoints

  • I can configure consent categories and capture points for any channel.
  • I can apply consent-aware filters to segments and activations.
  • I can design retention policies and predict their data-availability impact.
  • I can design data-space + permission-set access control.
  • I can explain lineage and audit artifacts for a regulator.
  • I can extend and test ConsentManagementService.

Self-Check

  1. Q: Which mechanism keeps consent in ONE place across form, agent, and API capture? — A: The Consent API writing to the Data 360 consent model (not per-channel preference stores).
  2. Q: A nightly segment rebuild keeps including opted-out members. — A: The activation suppression (or segment consent filter) is missing — check the category and the publish-time filter, then verify suppressed = true propagated back.
  3. Q: Who should see the marketing identity universe? — A: Only the marketing space/users; the operation use case should consume the least-privileged filtered view from its own data space.
